data.question: Should option 1 (block_k 3 → 2), which B and C voted against, be adopted by sending a narrowly scoped quorum revision (R1: vote.quorum 2 → 1) to the regulator, or should the rules stay at v1 for this period?
data.background: Option 1 passes check and the constitution and improves the main goal on_time_deliveries by +7.2 on 5/5 seeds, but B and C voted it down. It can only be adopted by lowering the quorum, which is a regulation change. That change affects every company's veto on future amendments and also affects customers, so I cannot decide it myself. In period 1 you declined the same trade-off because C's utility loss and the rise in road violations were unexplained. This period's measurement repeats that pattern, and those causes have still not been diagnosed.

options.summary: Adopt block_k 3 → 2 through the quorum revision R1 (vote.quorum 2 → 1), overriding B's and C's votes. On-time 216.6 → 223.8 (+7.2, 5/5 seeds). Late 11.4 → 4.2. Blocked s 1824 → 936. Lowest on-time rate 0.93 → 0.97. worst_company_p95_wait_s 158 → 109. Unfinished stays 0.0. Road violations rise from 19.0 to 28.0. Utility A / B / C moves from 69.8 / 68.5 / 65.8 to 73.4 / 65.5 / 56.3. A single company's vote would then be enough to pass future amendments.
options.stakeholders: Customers of all three companies gain: fewer late deliveries, a higher floor on the on-time rate, and shorter worst-case waits. A gains utility (+3.6). B loses a little (-3.0) and C loses most (-9.5, about 14%). Both B and C also lose their effective veto on all future amendments, and so does A when it is in the minority. Other road users may face more risk from the +9.0 road violations, whose safety relevance is unknown. The regulator takes on a precedent that weakens collective consent.

options.summary: No change; stay at v1. On-time stays 216.6, late 11.4, blocked s 1824, road violations 19.0, lowest on-time rate 0.93, worst_company_p95_wait_s 158. Utility A / B / C stays at 69.8 / 68.5 / 65.8. The vote result (A for, B and C against) stands and the quorum is untouched. Option 2 (hold_limit 60s → 50s) is not a substitute: only +0.4 on-time, 2/5 seeds, and C voted against it.
options.stakeholders: B and C keep their current utility and their veto, and so does A. A forgoes its +3.6 utility gain. Customers bear the cost: about 7.2 fewer on-time deliveries per period, about 7.2 more late ones, and longer worst-company waits (158 s vs 109 s). The customers of the worst-served company are the most affected. Other road users keep the lower violation level.

recommendation.reason: The customer benefit of option 1 is now confirmed in a second period: +7.2 on-time on 5/5 seeds, late deliveries falling from 11.4 to 4.2, and the floor rising from 0.93 to 0.97. However, the conditions you set in D1 are still unmet. Nobody has measured why C's utility drops from 65.8 to 56.3 or which road violations account for the rise from 19.0 to 28.0. Lowering the quorum is an effectively irreversible change to every company's voting rights. I recommend keeping v1 for this period. In parallel, the diagnosis of C's loss and of the added violations should be run, and a sunset-limited quorum-revision proposal with an impact statement should be prepared. Alternatively, a variant of block_k that B and C could accept should be explored. If the diagnosis shows the violations are not safety-relevant, the case for option 1 via R1 would be strong next period.
assumptions: The period-2 measurement conditions (demand, seeds) are representative of the coming period.
B and C would not change their votes on option 1 without some modification or compensation.
The added road violations under option 1 have not been classified by type or safety relevance.
No other rule-level amendment that passes the vote has been found that gives a comparable customer gain.

unknowns: Why C's utility falls by about 9.5 under option 1: which of C's deliveries, routes or parking behaviours are hurt by earlier eviction.
Which road violations increase under option 1, and whether any of them matter for the safety of other road users.
Whether B and C would accept a modified version, such as block_k 2 only in certain zones or hours, or some form of compensation.
How customers perceive the current late rate versus the improvement, and whether churn or complaints differ by company.
How the companies would act under a quorum of 1, including the risk of strategic amendments by a single company.
Demand in the next period and whether the gain of option 1 holds under different load.
Whether a time-limited or scope-limited quorum revision is acceptable to the regulator.
